packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

Layout survey: Two upright views of a tall narrow fragment, probably opposite faces. Both carry densely written brown text, now very faint in many places. In image-001 there is a narrow separate text strip at left and a wider principal area; the latter sometimes appears divided into two columns, but continuations across its middle are uncertain. Numerous enlarged dark words have red paragraph initials and red horizontal emphasis strokes. Additional smaller words are red-underlined. This may distinguish lemmata from explanatory text, but I cannot securely assign every span to either category. Image-002 is much more abraded and has a separate strip at right. Cuts, folds, discoloration, and holes obscure text. No secure running title. No clearly readable interlinear addition. A modern rectangular stamp occurs at the bottom of image-002; it has not been read or used.

Selected readings, preserving physical crop lines. The line numbering below belongs to the named derived images, counted from their top, not to the full photographs. These crops overlap; repetitions are not additional text.

Coverage and limitations: This packet does not yield a secure connected Latin passage for me. The tentative words above are letter-level readings with visible uncertainty, not a reconstruction. Image-001 was surveyed and its middle/lower principal writing enlarged; image-002 was surveyed but not transcribed. The other headings, upper writing, narrow peripheral columns, and most explanatory prose remain unread. I cannot distinguish a deletion from the red emphasis strokes with certainty, though their repeated placement makes emphasis plausible. Better contrast imaging might help; higher magnification alone did not resolve the faded strokes sufficiently. Do not use these uncertain lemmata as verified source-matching anchors.
